key_insight: Hard math prompts can jump from unsolved to solved, and higher early-generation entropy in failed rollouts signals failures closer to that transition.
engineering_relevance: NAPO turns otherwise uninformative all-failure rollout groups into training signals, improving hard-prompt learning under fixed rollout budgets.
method: Measure time-to-first-positive (TTFP) to analyze first-solution events.
Rank failed rollouts in unsolved groups using an early-branching driver.
Integrate graded negative advantages into GRPO where standard group-relative updates vanish.
evidence_signal: Under fixed rollout budgets, NAPO accelerates early solution discovery and improves Pass@256 by 10.0 points on AIME24 and 6.6 points on AIME2025.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether the entropy-based signal generalizes beyond the evaluated math settings.
paper_title: What Drives the Zero-to-One Jump? Diagnosing and Steering Hard-Prompt Learning in RLVR
